title: Stereo USB Audio Interface
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a stereo USB audio interface.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a stereo USB audio interface with stereo line input and stereo line output.

fixed_requirements.requirement: It provides stereo line input and stereo line output.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a stereo USB audio interface with stereo line input and stereo line output.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The USB side is implemented with either a USB-capable MCU or a USB audio bridge; the brief permits either and mandates neither.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: USB-capable MCU or USB audio bridge plus an audio codec

fixed_requirements.requirement: An audio codec is used alongside the USB-capable MCU or bridge.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Use a USB-capable MCU or USB audio bridge plus an audio codec supporting at least 24-bit/48 kHz operation.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The codec must support at least 24-bit / 48 kHz operation. This is a floor; the brief names no converter architecture and no upper limit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: an audio codec supporting at least 24-bit/48 kHz operation

fixed_requirements.requirement: Anti-alias / reconstruction components must be included, and they must be the ones the codec vendor recommends — so this requirement is discharged against the selected codec's own documentation, not against a generic filter.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Include anti-alias/reconstruction components recommended by the codec vendor

fixed_requirements.requirement: A low-jitter audio clock strategy must be included. The brief requires a strategy, not any named clock source, topology, or master/slave direction.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Include anti-alias/reconstruction components recommended by the codec vendor, a low-jitter audio clock strategy

fixed_requirements.requirement: ESD must be handled at USB.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Include anti-alias/reconstruction components recommended by the codec vendor, a low-jitter audio clock strategy, ESD at USB

fixed_requirements.requirement: The analog supplies must be quiet.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Include anti-alias/reconstruction components recommended by the codec vendor, a low-jitter audio clock strategy, ESD at USB, and quiet analog supplies.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Switching power must be kept away from the codec and from the analog connectors — a placement and partitioning constraint, not only a schematic one. It constrains switching power wherever it is used; it does not itself require that a switching converter be present.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Keep switching power away from the codec and analog connectors.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Four layers are preferred — the brief states a preference, not a mandated count.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Keep switching power away from the codec and analog connectors. Four layers are preferred.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Stated requirements are authoritative; where the brief is open, the design agent makes and documents reasonable engineering decisions instead of inventing hidden user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

fixed_requirements.requirement: This repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic must not accumulate in the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

open_decisions.decision: Whether the USB side is a USB-capable MCU (with firmware) or a dedicated USB audio bridge, and which specific device.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief explicitly offers both options with 'or' and names no part; the trade (firmware burden, class compliance, clock control, BOM) is left entirely to the design agent.

open_decisions.decision: Which audio codec is selected, its converter architecture, and its package, digital audio interface format and control interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief constrains the codec only by 'at least 24-bit/48 kHz' and names no vendor, part, architecture, package, or interface.

open_decisions.decision: Sample rates and bit depths actually supported above the stated floor, and whether multiple rates or rate families are supported.
open_decisions.why_open: 'at least 24-bit/48 kHz' sets a minimum; the brief says nothing about a maximum or about additional rates.

open_decisions.decision: USB speed, USB specification revision targeted, audio class model (class-compliant vs. driver-based), and descriptor/endpoint structure.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names USB and ESD at USB but is silent on speed, revision, class compliance, and host driver strategy; stereo 24-bit/48 kHz in and out does not by itself force a speed grade.

open_decisions.decision: USB connector type, orientation, and mounting style.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief never names a connector; it only requires a USB interface with ESD handling.

open_decisions.decision: Audio connector type and count for the stereo line input and stereo line output, and whether input and output share a connector family.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies stereo line in and stereo line out as functions only, and refers to 'analog connectors' with no type, pinout, or panel arrangement stated.

open_decisions.decision: Clock topology: crystal vs. packaged oscillator vs. recovered/PLL/rate-converted clocking, which device is audio clock master, and the phase-noise target that makes the strategy 'low-jitter'.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a low-jitter audio clock strategy but prescribes no source, no master/slave direction, and no jitter figure.

open_decisions.decision: Power source: bus-powered from USB, externally powered, or both; any USB current budget that follows; and whether VBUS presence is sensed at all.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on where power comes from and on unplug behaviour; it only constrains where switching power may be placed if it exists.

open_decisions.decision: Rail count, rail voltages, and regulator topology per domain (linear vs. switching) for digital, analog, and any bias rails, plus whether a switching converter exists on the board at all.
open_decisions.why_open: 'quiet analog supplies' states a goal with no voltages, no noise or PSRR figures, and no regulator type; the switching-power constraint bites only if a switcher is used, so an all-linear tree is not excluded.

open_decisions.decision: ESD protection scheme at USB: device type, placement, capacitance budget against the differential pair, and whether protection extends to the audio connectors.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names ESD at USB as a stressor to handle, not a component or an immunity level, and says nothing about the audio ports.

open_decisions.decision: Grounding and return-path strategy: unified vs. partitioned analog/digital ground, where and how domains join, and how USB and any switching returns are steered away from analog returns.
open_decisions.why_open: 'ground return control' is a listed stressor and the switching-power constraint implies partitioning, but the brief prescribes no grounding scheme.

open_decisions.decision: Whether the preferred four-layer count is adopted, and the stackup that follows: layer ordering and assignment, dielectric and copper weights, and the differential impedance target and tolerance for the USB pair.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says four layers are preferred — a preference, not a mandate — and the metadata calls 4 the likely layer count; no impedance, material, or layer assignment is given, so both the count and the stackup are the design agent's to choose and justify.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting hole pattern, connector edge placement, and any enclosure or panel fit.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no mechanical constraint of any kind.

open_decisions.decision: Analog signal conditioning around the codec: nominal line level, input attenuation or gain, buffering, single-ended vs. differential handling, AC coupling and DC bias.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires vendor-recommended anti-alias/reconstruction components but says nothing about levels, gain structure, or buffering.

open_decisions.decision: Whether any feature beyond stereo line in/out exists — headphone drive, level or mute controls, indicators, monitoring/loopback, firmware update path, or test points.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief describes only stereo line input and stereo line output; it neither requires nor forbids anything further.

open_decisions.decision: Manufacturing choices: fabricator and assembly process class, minimum trace/space and via geometry, single- vs. double-sided assembly, and panelization.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states a layer preference only and names no vendor, process class, or assembly constraint.

open_decisions.decision: Which audio performance figures (SNR, THD+N, crosstalk, channel separation) the design commits to, and how they are to be verified.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief sets a resolution and sample-rate floor but states no performance targets or measurement conditions.
